```{r setup}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 13))
dl <- fread("tissue_pool_dilution/dilution_factor_mex42.tsv")
dl[, family := fcase(status == "pass", "balanced", status == "fail", "unbalanced", default = "no tier-A sites")]
both <- dl[!is.na(f_het) & !is.na(f_alt) & family != "no tier-A sites"]
summ <- dl[family != "no tier-A sites", .(
  samples = .N, f_het = median(f_het, na.rm = TRUE), f_alt = median(f_alt, na.rm = TRUE),
  ref_bg = median(ref_bg, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = family]
corr <- both[, .(samples = .N, r = cor(f_het, f_alt)), by = family]
diag_cluster <- both[family == "unbalanced" & f_alt < 0.65 & abs(f_alt - f_het) < 0.2]
```

## The question

Each BC2S3 sample is a tissue pool: one leaf punch from each of six plants of one NIL, assumed to give equimolar DNA
(`docs/TERMINOLOGY.md`). The sample introgression dosage check (`docs/decisions.md`, 2026-10-11) splits the 42
mexicana families of run 1273053 into two sets: families with **balanced tissue pools**
(their samples read the expected ALT in donor segments) and with **unbalanced tissue pools** (too little ALT). The
deficit is one-sided: no family reads too much ALT. Random unequal plant contributions would push dosage both ways, so
something lowers the donor reads systematically. Candidates: dilution (other tissue or B73 DNA in the pool), selection
against carriers during line development, mapping bias.

## The dilution factor

For each sample and donor-segment state, the dilution factor is the observed ALT read frequency divided by the expected
one; the expected one is the read-weighted ALT frequency of the families with balanced tissue pools (HET segments
41.1 %, ALT segments 86.3 %). States with fewer than 100 reads are left out.

- **ALT segments** (donor allele in all six plants): the factor is about 1 in a balanced pool and falls with any
  admixed tissue. It is the clean dilution measure.
- **HET segments** (the six plants segregate): the factor varies by segregation inside the pool even without dilution.
- **Dilution** lowers both by the same factor (the diagonal). Selection and mapping bias act on loci, not on the whole
  sample, so they do not keep the two equal.

```{r summary}
knitr::kable(summ,
  digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 1),
  col.names = c("families", "samples", "HET factor, median", "ALT factor, median", "REF background, median ALT %")
)
```

```{r plot}
ggplot(both, aes(f_het, f_alt, colour = family)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 1.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(balanced = "#1b9e77", unbalanced = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c(balanced = "balanced tissue pools", unbalanced = "unbalanced tissue pools"), name = NULL
  ) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1.65), ylim = c(0, 1.65)) +
  labs(
    title = "Dilution factor per BC2S3 sample, mexicana chr10",
    subtitle = sprintf("%d samples with >= 100 reads in both HET and ALT segments", nrow(both)),
    x = "HET segments (observed / expected ALT)", y = "ALT segments (observed / expected ALT)"
  )
```

## What it shows

- **Balanced families:** ALT factor near 1 (median `r round(summ[family == "balanced", f_alt], 2)`), HET factor
  spread by segregation; the two are unrelated (r = `r round(corr[family == "balanced", r], 2)`).
- **Unbalanced families:** both factors lower (medians `r round(summ[family == "unbalanced", f_het], 2)` and
  `r round(summ[family == "unbalanced", f_alt], 2)`) and moving together (r = `r round(corr[family == "unbalanced", r], 2)`).
  `r nrow(diag_cluster)` samples sit on the diagonal with an ALT factor below 0.65: diluted pools.
- **REF background is the same** in both (`r summ[family == "balanced", ref_bg]` %). Tissue from another donor family
  would raise it; B73 or recurrent-parent tissue would not. So the dilution, where present, is B73-like.

## Limits

- Only `r nrow(both)` of `r nrow(dl)` samples have both factors: many samples carry no ALT segment on chr10.
- Selection is not tested here; it needs the deficit per region across families (recurring low windows, stronger in
  ALT than in HET segments).
- One chromosome, one taxon.
